Always read your character sheet fully before the session one. Yep, especially your McLovin`.
Take notes during the session, especially names of NPCs of course if you want to know who will make your party unconsious next time.

Always recap the last session at the start of the next one. If you don't, your players will completely forget the name of the main villain but perfectly remember the exact voice you gave a random goblin named Bob.
Respect the table rules and the DM's final rulings. But don't forget to argue if something looks wrong!
Keep your phone away during play. Checking your texts mid-combat legally means your character is having an existential crisis about a glowing brick, giving monsters advantage to hit you.
Remember that failing some rolls makes the story more interesting and harder for DM.
Better know what your turn looks like before it starts. Especially if your turn looks like a panicked octopus trying to parallel park while eating a taco
Remember, you can slice your movement into pieces like a goblin birthday cake instead of running all at once.
Ready an action for specific triggers instead of rushing in blind. But second variant sound's more realistic.
Track your concentration spells carefully every turn. Seriously - CONCENTRATE on it!
Interact with one object for free on your turn, like opening a door or crying for the DM's help.
Tie your backstory directly to the campaign setting if it's possible. If not - the DM will kidnap you into his basement.
Rolling a natural '1' on a stealth check means you didn't just fail. You loudly announced your exact coordinates and social security number to the goblins.
If it fits in the Bag of Holding, it belongs to the party. If it's a pillar holding up the dungeon roof, it still fits if you push it hard enough.
As a Wizard, your highest stat is Intelligence, but your most important stat is 'how fast you can hide behind the Barbarian when the initiative is rolled'.
Threatening the barkeeper is a great way to find out that every retired adventurer 10+lvl in a 50-mile radius works as a dishwasher at that exact tavern.
When the DM asks 'Are you sure?', the correct answer is never 'Yes'. The correct answer is an immediate apology and a total rewrite of your strategy.
Seducing the Dragon is a valid strategy until you succeed and realize you have to plan a whole wedding and a first wedding night in the Elemental Plane of Fire.
A locked wooden door is a puzzle. A locked wooden door after the Barbarian gets bored is a collection of very loud woods.
If you read the Monster Manual mid-combat, the monster suddenly gains a laser cannon. The DM makes the rules, and the rules say STOP CHEATING!
Turning into a Goldfish during a high-stakes stealth mission is technically a choice. Not a good choice, but a choice.
Your character must have a 'reason' to adventure. 'Being an eldery lone man, who hates people' is a great reason to stay home and guard the cabbage patch.
Buying 50 feet of 'Hempen Rope' is mandatory. You will never use it for climbing, but you will use it to tie up a suspicious goblin baker who told you that you know his name - Gobter White.
Your Oath of Devotion protects your soul, but it does not protect you from the Rogue stealing your gold to buy 'holy water' from a suspicious vendor.
If the Rogue says 'I got this!' - find a bunker immediately. If the Wizard says 'I got this!' - whrite a new character sheet.
Having **Darkvision** means you can see in the dark, not that you can see through solid walls. Stop asking what is inside the stone sarcophagus.
If you start a brawl in a tavern, the local guard will arrive in exactly two rounds. If the town is being attacked by a someone, guards are suddenly dissapear.
Be nice to the Cleric. They control the literal boundary between your character sheet staying on the table or going directly into the bin.
The Ranger is an expert survivalist. If he suggest eating the glowing blue-violet mushrooms, he is either testing your immune system or thoroughly bored.
Rolling a 20 on Intimidation while playing a 3-foot-tall Halfling means the Orc chieftain isn't scared of your weapon - he's terrified of your size.
As a Sorcerer, 'room temperature' is defined as whatever temperature the hallway becomes after you cast Fireball in a enclosed 10-foot space.
Offering the Goblin king a shiny copper piece and a half-eaten sandwich works 40% of the time, which is a terrifyingly high statistic.
Your Monk can catch arrows out of the air. This does not mean you should play dodgeball with the local elven archer regiment to earn quick coin.
The main quest to save the kingdom is important, but buying a pet goose and teaching it how to wear a tiny top hat is always the true priority.
Your Patron called. He don't want your soul anymore. He WANT you to stop texting them at 3:00 AM asking if Eldritch Blast works on walls!.
When the DM sighs, takes off their glasses, and rubs the bridge of their nose, you haven't won the encounter. You have just initiated Phase 2 really quick.
